(Ref: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/pull/35216)

workarounds.symptom: Console: saved changes stay "Unsaved" because editors compare JSON by key order
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(console): acknowledge canonical saved JSON without losing edits. Target files: backend/app/api/routes/v1/agents.py, backend/app/services/agent_runner.py, backend/app/services/workflow_evals.py. Saving a draft could leave the Builder or dataset grading marked unsaved when JSONB reordered keys or the server filled defaults. The Builder could save twice and block draft testing; equivalent remote updates could show conflicts, and unchanged routine folder settings could request approval again. (Ref: https://github.com/vstorm-co/agenticos/pull/2923)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug] ctx.debug/info/warning/error raise RuntimeError in background tasks (session is not available)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(context): allow background task logging without a session. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/context.py, tests/server/test_context.py. - allow `Context.log()` to resolve the background task's captured session key when no live MCP session exists - keep server-side logging and skip only the unavailable client notification back-channel - add a regression test for `ctx.info()` in a worker context (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/5806)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug] Azure Responses bridge inherits chat-era api-version, rejected by Azure (needs >= 2025-03-01-preview)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(azure): use supported API versions for Responses requests. Target files: litellm/llms/azure/responses/transformation.py, tests/unit/llms/azure/response/test_azure_transformation.py. Azure gpt-6 chat requests that use tools get sent to Azure's Responses API behind the scenes, and they were carrying over an older API version that Azure refuses there, so users got a 400 error. Now an API version that is too old for Responses is swapped for the default Responses version, so these requests go through (Ref: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51116)

workarounds.symptom: `createInngestAgent`: post-run scores name a span that is never stored
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(inngest): save agent scores on the stored agent run span. Target files: packages/core/src/loop/test-utils/aimock/scenarios/scorers-call-time.scenario.test.ts, workflows/inngest/src/durable-agent/create-inngest-agentic-workflow.ts, .changeset/cold-laws-hunt.md. Scores from a `createInngestAgent` agent pointed at a span that is never stored, so the agent run in a trace showed no scores. The score event also lost the agent and the `runId`. The score now points at the run's `agent_run` span, the same as for a plain `Agent`. (Ref: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/30016)

workarounds.symptom: Error in llm chat due to invalid key \e[d from case conversion in key bindings (Windows 11)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Skip invalid readline arrow-key bindings on Windows, fixes #585. Target files: llm/cli.py. The win32 branch in `chat()` passes GNU-readline syntax (`bind -x '\e[D: backward-char'`) to `readline.parse_and_bind()`. On Windows that is pyreadline3, which lowercases key descriptions and raises `IndexError: Not a valid key` for escape sequences like `\e[D` — exactly the traceback in this issue. Reporters in the thread confirmed chat starts normally once the bindings are removed, and pyreadline3 provides its own arrow-key handling, so t... (Ref: https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1809)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Native FlashInfer produces garbage output with BF16 Q and non-unit q_scale
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [Bugfix] Apply the layer q_scale only to FP8 queries in FlashInfer. Target files: vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py, tests/models/quantization/test_fp8.py, tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py. When the query that reaches FlashInfer is BF16/FP16, `FlashInferImpl.forward` still passed the layer's FP8 query scale (`layer._q_scale_float`) to the kernel. FlashInfer multiplies the softmax scale by it, so with a checkpoint that has a non-unit `q_scale` the attention output is wrong. This PR adds `FlashInferImpl.... (Ref: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64329)

workarounds.symptom: hindsight-api exits at start-up with UnicodeEncodeError when stdout is redirected on Windows
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(api): a redirected stdout on Windows no longer stops the server at start-up. Target files: hindsight-api-slim/hindsight_api/admin/cli.py, hindsight-api-slim/hindsight_api/main.py, hindsight-api-slim/hindsight_api/utils.py. **Problem.** Before Python 3.15, a redirected stdout on Windows (`hindsight-api > hindsight.log`) uses the ANSI code page (cp1252, cp949). It cannot encode the banner logo's block characters, so the server exited with `UnicodeEncodeError` before it served anything. (Ref: https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/pull/6508)

workarounds.symptom: `llm openai endpoint add` writes unparseable YAML when the existing list is indented
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Preserve YAML layout when adding OpenAI endpoints. Target files: llm/default_plugins/openai_models.py, tests/test_openai_endpoint_add.py. Adding an endpoint to an indented block list wrote the new entry at column zero, leaving `extra-openai-models.yaml` unparseable. Appending after an explicit `...` document end marker caused the same failure, so subsequent model-loading commands stopped working. (Ref: https://github.com/simonw/llm/pull/1865)

workarounds.symptom: Terminal tool: false positive blocking npm update/install commands containing 'vite'
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Terminal no longer refuses harmless commands that only mention a dev server (salvage #150773, #108599, #95481). Target files: tools/terminal_tool_guards.py, tests/tools/test_terminal_guard_command_position.py. The terminal tool refused harmless commands that merely mention a dev server (`grep -rn uvicorn .`, `ls node_modules/vite`, `npm install nodemon`), telling the model to run them in the background. Those now run; commands that actually start a server are refused exactly as before. (Ref: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/153382)
